references.text: The Midianites came and destroyed the crops in the land, and Israel was oppressed by foreign nations who took the fruit of their labor.
Israel suffered under the oppression of the Midianites, which serves as an example of the curse that foreign nations would take the fruits of their work.
Warning that enemies will eat what they have sown, as part of the covenant curses for disobedience.
Prophecy that foreigners will devour Israel's strength and wealth because of their apostasy.
Others will eat what Israel has worked for, fulfilling the curse.
Prophecy that they will sow but not reap, because others will take the fruit of their labor.
Further explanation of the same theme: a foreign nation will consume the harvest and all they have worked for.
